text.p: - Fresh snow caused serious traffic problems in Slovenia on Tuesday.
- Slovenian employers and unions to continue talks on an overhaul of a general collective agreement on work benefits.

- "Spring coalition" of rightist parties, comprising conservative People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, has yet to determine its candidate for the presidency of the new parliament. The parties, which together won 45 out of 90 parliametary seats in a November 10 general election, hopes to form the next government.
- Just seven women were elected to the new parliament, down from 12 in the last election four years ago.
- The government Office for the Prevention of Money Laundering said the value of suspicious money transactions in Slovenia since the beginning of 1995 had reached 19 billion tolars ($136.7 million).

- Slovenian president Milan Kucan opened a two-day meeting of government representatives of the Alpe-Adria community, comprising Slovenia, Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia, in the port city of Portoroz on Tuesday.
- The strike of most employees of troubled shoe factory Peko over unpaid October wages continued on Tuesday.
- Bank Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor may take a 30 percent share in bank Hipotekarna Banka Brezice.
